core_job: Put every leg of one trip (flights, trains, buses, ferries, car hire, transfers, stays) into one time-ordered itinerary. Each leg has structured places and local times in that place's own time zone. Everything stays on the phone and works offline, with no account. Primary user: an independent traveller booking a 3–14 day multi-leg trip across several sites.
signature: Gap Check: an on-device check of the whole trip, against bundled offline GeoNames cities5000 (CC BY 4.0) and OurAirports IATA data with IANA time zones. It flags: (1) nights with no bed, shown on a nights strip (an overnight journey counts as covered); (2) legs that don't connect, either a different city more than 50 km away or a different airport 5–50 km away, e.g. GOI vs GOX; (3) overlaps and tight connections, compared in absolute time across zones; (4) an airport or station arrival with no way to a stay more than 15 km away; (5) two stays booked for the same night; (6) no way home (Info only). Each finding has a 'Fill this gap' hand-off to Booking.com, Airbnb or Google Maps, prefilled from the gap, and the booking can then be recorded back into the trip. Competitor listings read through the keyless iTunes API: TripIt, Wanderlog and Tripsy need accounts or email import. Their listing text does not mention night coverage or wrong-airport chaining. Tripsy mentions travel-time buffers. How these apps actually behave is not verified.
